I first tried Stranded Deep a couple of years ago on Xbox Series S and came away pretty disappointed. The performance and visuals just weren’t there. Frame rates often felt like 25 to 30 fps, and things like birds flying or trees falling looked almost like stop-motion. On top of that, early resources felt too limited, which made it hard to get into the game at all.

I recently gave it another shot after moving to PC, and the difference is huge. Gameplay is smooth, with a stable frame rate (I cap at 120), and the overall experience feels far more polished. Resources are still something you have to work for, but they no longer feel frustratingly scarce. The updates over the past couple of years have added solid quality-of-life improvements and noticeable performance gains.

This time I’m genuinely enjoying it. I’ve already put about 15 hours in over a few days, focusing on gathering materials, crafting tools, and getting ready to sail between islands to push the story forward.

Overall, the improvements have completely changed my view of the game. What once felt clunky and underwhelming is now a fun, engaging survival experience that I’d happily recommend to anyone who enjoys the genre.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (73%): players praise the graphics and co-op, but bugs and crashes are the main complaint.
Recent reviews are far less positive, so check current feedback before buying.

details.text: Recent reviews complain more about gameplay and combat, at 15% against 9% all time, and bugs and crashes are a little higher too.
Players with the fewest hours are far less positive than veterans, with only 40% of them positive.
